steps.body: Splitting a whole into **halves** means cutting it into 2 equal parts. Each part is called a **half**. Both halves must be the same size — a big piece and a small piece aren't halves.

widget.prompt: If you split a whole into halves, how many equal parts do you get?

commonErrors.feedback: Splitting means cutting into more than 1 piece — halves means 2 equal parts.
4 equal parts is fourths (quarters), not halves. Halves is 2 parts.

predict.reveal: 'Half' means the whole shared into exactly TWO equal parts — three equal parts make thirds, no matter how fair the cut.

explanationVariants: One of 2 equal parts is called a half.

steps.body: You can split a shape in half in different ways — straight down the middle, or corner to corner — as long as the two pieces are equal in size.

widget.prompt: A square is cut corner to corner into two triangles. Are the two triangles halves?

options.label: Yes, if they're equal in size
options.feedback: Yes — cutting corner to corner gives two equal triangles, which are halves.

options.label: No, only straight cuts count
options.feedback: The cut direction doesn't matter — what matters is the two parts are equal in size.

options.label: No, they're not squares anymore
options.feedback: Shape can change; halves is about equal SIZE, not keeping the same shape.

steps.body: Two halves always make one whole again. If you put the two equal pieces back together, you get the original shape back.

widget.prompt: A rectangle is split into halves. How many equal pieces are there?

commonErrors.feedback: That's fourths (quarters). Halves means 2 equal pieces.
Splitting means more than 1 piece — halves gives 2.

steps.body: Halves are 2 equal parts of a whole — any cut direction works if the parts match in size.
takeaways: Halves means splitting into 2 equal parts.
Each equal part is called a half.
Unequal parts are never halves, no matter the number.
